title: Chicken Tikka Masala
subtitle: Marinated grilled chicken in a creamy tomato curry sauce
excerpt: Chicken pieces marinated in spiced yoghurt, grilled until charred at the edges, then simmered in a rich tomato and cream sauce seasoned with garam masala and coriander. Britain's most popular curry.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken tikka masala is widely considered Britain's most popular dish, regularly topping polls of British favourites. Its exact origin is disputed: some claim it was invented by a chef in Glasgow who added a tomato and cream sauce to chicken tikka to please a customer who found the dish too dry; others trace it to the Bangladeshi restaurant kitchens of London's Brick Lane in the 1970s. Whatever its origin, it is now firmly part of British food culture. The dish is a hybrid: chicken tikka (marinated, charred chicken) is genuinely Indian; the masala sauce that surrounds it was developed specifically for the British market. The charring of the chicken before it enters the sauce is what distinguishes a proper chicken tikka masala from a plain chicken curry.

recipeTools.notes: A wide saucepan for the masala sauce.
A baking tray for grilling the tikka.

content.text: The chicken must be grilled under high heat until the marinade chars in patches: this char is the flavour of tikka. Do not skip this step or the result will be a plain chicken curry rather than a tikka masala. Make the sauce while the chicken marinates. The sauce can be made a day ahead and reheated with the chicken stirred through at the end.

items.preparation: half for marinade, half for sauce

content.text: Mix the yoghurt with half the garlic, half the ginger, ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, sweet paprika, and half the salt. Add the chicken and coat thoroughly. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.

Heat the oil in a wide pan. Fry the onion for 12 minutes until deep golden. Add the remaining garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes, chilli powder, and the remaining salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the tomato has cooked through.
Thread the chicken onto skewers or spread on a baking tray. Grill under a very hot grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until charred in patches and cooked through.

Stir the cream and garam masala into the tomato sauce. Add the grilled chicken pieces. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Taste for seasoning. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with naan or basmati rice.
